summary: Intermittent async-embed ingest dtype/shape mismatch causing rerank top-k collapse and latency spikes
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent severe reranking quality degradation (top-k collapse) accompanied by backend latency spikes. Impact: NovaSearch search relevance drops to near-zero on affected requests; several production queries return duplicate scores / truncated results and client-facing timeouts. Environment: Production (us-east-1) on Dedicated cluster (reserved GPUs), traffic proxying through api-gateway to embeddings ingest pipeline with async enrich/shims enabled. Timeline: 2026-03-09 customer first reported sporadic relevance regressions; support triaged and opened this ticket 2026-03-10 after reproducing on a small traffic window. Observed: Errors are not uniform — only ~0.6% of embed->rerank flows show the failure pattern, but those have outsized customer impact because they hit high-traffic endpoints. Failures coincide with short latency spikes from reranker pods (p95 -> 2.5s) and 5xxs in the rerank service. Hypothesis: asynchrony in the ingest shim leads to a mixture of float32 and uint8/quantized payloads arriving at reranker; a silent casting/padding bug in the serving-runtime quant path interprets smaller-length vectors as zero-padded high-similarity vectors, collapsing top-k diversity and triggering a CPU fallback causing latency. This ticket centralizes investigation, mitigation, and a follow-up plan.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send two batched embedding requests from client UUIDs A and B within 10ms of each other using async-upload shim (the customer's pattern).
2) For latent repro, alternate precision: one request as float32 array, next request as uint8 packed bytes (customer uses mixed client SDKs).
3) Route both to embeddings-ingest with async enrichment enabled; observe metrics on reranker p95 and top-k diversity for the same query template.
4) Reproduce reliably by adding deliberate 5-15ms jitter on ingest worker to emulate async sharding behaviour.
logs: [2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] reranker-0 pod: WARNING: topk output contains 8 identical scores; returned_ids=[123,124,125,126]
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] serving-runtime: INFO: received embedding payload metadata{"dtype":"uint8","length":1536} (note: upstream declared float32 for other batch)
[2026-03-09T18:12:04Z] serving-runtime: ERROR: kv-cache missstorm + quant_cast path triggered cpu_fallback (trace_id=tr-9b3f). stack=RuntimeError: quant_cast: unexpected shape after decode
investigation: 2026-03-10 - Reproduced locally against staging by replaying customer's trace; confirmed mixed-dtype payloads in single batch can be produced by customer's async shim.

Checked embedding-schema validator in the ingest path: it tolerates dtype mismatch but does not cast or normalize when async metadata shim is present (intended), which allowed mixed encodings to proceed downstream.

Instrumented serving-runtime to log incoming dtype/length per sample; observed runs where uint8-packed embeddings were decoded but length field mismatch produced zero-padding at the end of vector causing high cosine matches (simulated identical vectors).
Observed that when quant_cast path takes these malformed lengths, it triggers a slow CPU fallback in ~50ms of cases, increasing reranker processing time and causing p95 spikes.
Hypothesis validated: combination of async ingest reorder + missing per-sample schema enforcement + len/dtype mismatch -> both quality (top-k collapse) and latency (cpu fallback) issues.

Priority fix identified: enforce strict schema validation and per-sample casting at ingest boundary (fast-fail malformed payloads) and add defensive padding-trim logic in serving-runtime quant decoder.
comments: Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-10: Customer provided three example request traces and a reproduction harness; escalated to SRE/Engineering due to production impact.

SRE (Dion Ramirez) 2026-03-11: Spin up isolated traffic mirror for NovaSearch pattern; confirmed rerank p95 jumps when mirror enabled. Adding temporary traffic-sampling toggle to prevent full customer impact.

Eng (Ethan Clarke) 2026-03-11: Drafted quick mitigation: 1) disable async-shim feature flag for NovaSearch in edge config 2) patch ingest validator to reject mixed-dtype batches. Preparing PR for serving-runtime defensive trim. (PR referenced below)

Customer (Alex Liu, NovaSearch) 2026-03-11: Confirmed workaround when support toggled async-shim off; relevance returned to baseline for the mirrored traffic. Please advise on timeline for permanent fix and SDK changes.

Support (Maya Patel) 2026-03-12: Noted that disabling async-shim reduced error rate to ~0.03% (from ~0.6%) and p95 latencies are back within SLO. Proceeding to coordinate fix rollout with Eng and Customer Success.
resolution: Mitigation applied: feature-flagged async-shim disabled for NovaSearch (edge config) 2026-03-11 which materially reduced incidents. Engineering patch deployed to staging 2026-03-12: serving-runtime PR #2786 adds defensive padding-trim and strict per-sample dtype-length checks in quant decode path; ingest-validator updated to cast or reject mixed-dtype batches depending on customer config. Production rollout plan: canary rollout to 10% traffic 2026-03-14, full rollout 2026-03-16 after 48h monitoring. Follow-ups: 1) add SDK-level embedding-schema validation and unit tests (owner: SDK team) 2) include a regression test in nightly e2e ingestion->rerank pipeline (owner: QA) 3) Docs: update embed schema runbook and customer guidance for async ingestion patterns (owner: Solutions). Linked internal INT-4302 created to track postmortem and permanent monitoring alerts.
